t: You're on Garrick Street, in the City of Westminster. The street takes its name from David Garrick, the eighteenth-century British actor, playwright and theatre manager. Garrick influenced nearly all aspects of European theatre in his day, and he was a pupil and friend of Samuel Johnson. It was his appearance as Richard the Third in Shakespeare's play that made audiences and managers begin to take notice of him. His name here is a reminder of how much the stage mattered to this part of London.
